finding: @red-cup-engineering/http-server-core-service 0.1.1's Node start() transport does not route a rejected handler through the fetch handler's onError, so an over-limit request body answers plain-text 500 instead of the JSON 413 the Fetch transport gives
reproduction: createFetchHandler({ onError, resources: [{ match: "/p", methods: ["POST"], handler: async (ctx) => Response.json(await readJsonBody(ctx.request, { maxBytes: 1024 })) }] }) served two ways with the same 4KiB JSON body: the Fetch transport (calling the handler directly) answers 413 {"error":"request body exceeded 1024 bytes","isBodyReadError":true,"name":"BodyReadError"}; the Node transport (start({ fetch: handler })) answers 500 "Internal Server Error" as plain text. The repro uses no paid-pacing-intelligence-gateway code at all.
exposedBy: test/http-application.test.mjs in this gateway, which asserts the two transports agree on 400/415/413 for malformed bodies. Its 413 case fails on the Node transport for this reason; the other 33 tests in this package pass.
notDoneHere: Repairing and republishing @red-cup-engineering/http-server-core-service is a separate lot in that package's own custody, with its own consumers to re-pin; this gateway's offer migration did not cause the defect and does not paper over it.
